Oggi è previsto il secondo e ultimo giorno di riposo dopo l’amichevole con il Mgarr. Da domani la Lazio comincerà a preparare la gara di sabato alle 15 all’Olimpico, mentre Gattuso continua a riflettere sulle soluzioni disponibili.

Sutalo resterà fuori ancora a lungo e salterà sia il derby sia la finale di Supercoppa. Nel cuore della difesa servirà quindi spazio per un centrale utilizzato meno degli altri. Oliver è a quota 901 minuti; seguono l’ex Ajax con 597, Doekhi con 413 e Leite con 249.

Proprio l’impiego del portoghese a Napoli ha sorpreso. Ci si aspettava l’ingresso di Danilo, ma Gattuso ha scelto il mancino anche in considerazione delle caratteristiche di Hojlund. La Lazio si è così ritrovata con due centrali dal piede sinistro preferito. Per Diogo era una posizione nuova: non vi era mai stato impiegato né provato. Ha comunque risposto alla chiamata, come nelle altre occasioni avute in questa stagione.

It has been revealed that prima dell’infortunio alla mano, Doekhi sembrava un titolare inamovibile. Lo stop aveva poi consentito a Sutalo di salire nelle gerarchie. La decisione presa al Maradona, dove la sostituzione di un destro con un altro destro appariva la soluzione più immediata, ha riaperto il confronto tra Doekhi e Leite.

Il Lecce di Eusebio Di Francesco è un avversario capace di creare difficoltà. A Formello la sfida viene già considerata una trappola, forse per scaramanzia, forse perché è questa la convinzione nell’ambiente. La migliore difesa della Serie A è chiamata a confermarsi, ma la scelta dei centrali arriverà soltanto dopo il ritorno di Provstgaard, previsto mercoledì. Rinunciare al danese, soprannominato Iron Man, non sarebbe semplice, soprattutto con Sutalo indisponibile.

It has been revealed that L’esperimento di Napoli ha mostrato a Gattuso di poter contare anche sui centrali meno utilizzati. Resta aperta un’altra possibilità: Doekhi e Leite insieme dal primo minuto contro i giallorossi salentini. I due ex Union Berlino hanno giocato spesso fianco a fianco negli ultimi anni, anche se in una difesa a tre. Sabato sono stati schierati insieme a Formello nell’amichevole con il Mgarr; Leite ha anche segnato, grazie a una carambola fortunata.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany U21 will look to finish their international calendar on a positive note when they travel to Rijeka to face Croatia on Tuesday evening.
  • Antonio Di Salvo’s side have already secured qualification for the 2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship, but November’s fixtures against fellow qualifiers Belgium and Croatia represent an notable opportunity to measure themselves against some of Europe’s strongest teams at this level.
  • Germany suffered a disappointing 2-1 defeat to Belgium on Friday, leaving them with a point to prove as they prepare for another demanding encounter against a Croatian side that also topped its qualifying group.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany U21 will look to finish their international calendar on a positive note when they travel to Rijeka to face Croatia on Tuesday evening.

Antonio Di Salvo’s side have already secured qualification for the 2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship, but November’s fixtures against fellow qualifiers Belgium and Croatia represent an notable opportunity to measure themselves against some of Europe’s strongest teams at this level.

Germany suffered a disappointing 2-1 defeat to Belgium on Friday, leaving them with a point to prove as they prepare for another demanding encounter against a Croatian side that also topped its qualifying group.

Germany entered the November international break having secured their place at next summer’s European Championship, with three consecutive victories in their final qualifying matches ensuring direct qualification.

It has been revealed that however, their preparations for the tournament have not started entirely as planned. Despite enjoying plenty of possession and creating several promising opportunities, Germany were beaten 2-1 by Belgium in Essen on Friday.

Julien Duranville gave the visitors an early lead before Muhammed Damar equalised with an excellent free-kick in the 25th minute. Germany continued to create opportunities after the break, with Damar particularly unfortunate to hit the crossbar twice, but Romeo Vermant ultimately secured victory for Belgium.

The defeat highlighted an issue Di Salvo will be keen to address against Croatia: turning territorial dominance and promising attacking situations into goals.

Germany’s head coach has already indicated that the November fixtures are an opportunity to experiment with different approaches, particularly in their pressing game, while continuing to develop the team’s understanding ahead of next summer.

In a recent development, there have also been opportunities for several less-established members of the squad. Hennes Behrens and Cajetan Lenz made their U21 debuts against Belgium, while Maurice Krattenmacher and Louey Ben Farhat also received their first appearances at this level.

It has been revealed that germany will once again be without several notable names. Nicolo Tresoldi, who scored 10 goals during European Championship qualifying, suffered a concussion in training and has been ruled out of both November fixtures. Goalkeeper Mio Backhaus and defender Hendry Blank are also unavailable following injuries.

Furthermore, six players eligible for the U21s, including Said El Mala, Brajan Gruda, Tom Bischof and Lennart Karl, have been given opportunities with the senior national team.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, there is still considerable quality available to Di Salvo. Muhammed Damar will be one to watch following his impressive display against Belgium, while Paris Brunner and Dzenan Pejcinovic offer further attacking options.

Joshua Quarshie, who captained Germany against Belgium, and Nnamdi Collins will also be notable figures as the visitors look to improve defensively.

Croatia will provide a stern examination for Germany, having also secured qualification for next summer’s European Championship after an impressive qualifying campaign.

Ivica Olić’s side finished top of Group H with six victories, one draw and one defeat, collecting 19 points from their eight matches.

Their qualification was secured with a 3-1 victory over Hungary in September, while they subsequently finished their campaign with a 1-0 win away to Lithuania.

Tuesday’s encounter represents Croatia’s first major opportunity to begin preparations for the European Championship, with Olić keen to test his players against high-quality opposition.

The Croatian coach has spoken positively about facing Germany, describing them as one of the strongest teams at this age group alongside Spain. He also highlighted the quality of their young players, several of whom have already attracted attention from the senior national team.

In a recent development, there will be some notable absentees for the hosts, however. Šimun Hrgović and Marin Šotiček have joined Croatia’s senior squad for their Nations League fixtures, while injuries have also forced changes to Olić’s original selection.

Lovro Zvonarek is among the players expected to provide important quality in midfield, while Adriano Jagušić is another name worth monitoring after scoring five goals during the qualifying campaign.

Croatia will be particularly motivated to make a positive impression against one of Europe’s traditional youth football powerhouses, especially with the European Championship draw scheduled for November 26.

Croatia U21 (4-3-3): Pavlešić; Hodak, Prpić, Mlačić, Krušelj; Zvonarek, Pavić, Jagušić; Tunjić, Verinac, Canjuga.

Germany U21 (4-2-3-1): Seimen; Baum, Collins, Quarshie, Gechter; Lenz, Aseko; Kade, Damar, Brunner; Pejcinovic.

How Michael Carrick's Man United fell apart: Players' bust-up on flight back from Madrid, weakness in training and on touchline - and why dressing-room sources believe divided board 'hung him out to dry'

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 10:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:44 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • For the last two days, Michael Carrick has followed his familiar route towards Manchester United’s training base, nudging his black Land Rover past the security barrier at Carrington before 8am, and making his way into work just as he has for much of the last two decades as a player, coach and head coach at the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:44 EST, 12 November 2026.

For the last two days, Michael Carrick has followed his familiar route towards Manchester United’s training base, nudging his black Land Rover past the security barrier at Carrington before 8am, and making his way into work just as he has for much of the last two decades as a player, coach and head coach at the club.

While Carrick's fate has been decided by men in suits in Monaco and Manchester, he has put on his training gear and gone through the motions of coaching whichever players are left during the international break.

It has become increasingly apparent that Carrick was a dead man walking in the two weeks since the United board gave him a stay of execution and bought themselves time after the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last month.

Having effectively been brought in as a caretaker when United plucked him off the beach in Barbados in mid-January, he left much the same way: merely keeping the seat warm for Mauricio Pochettino in the chaotic days that have led to his sacking.

Sources close to the United dressing room believe Carrick has been ‘hung out to dry’ as United dithered over his future and then began a futile attempt to appoint Pochettino as his replacement in secret.

This is the story of how Carrick's United fell apart. It is the story of how disgruntled players aired their dirty laundry in public and clashed in private. It is the story of how the club's boardroom became the backdrop for an executive power struggle. And it is the story of how the magic touch that saw Carrick land the job permanently just five months ago deserted him...

Michael Carrick is out as Manchester United manager - just ten league games after guiding United to third and being handed a two-year contract.

Carrick has had to turn up as normal at Carrington this week even as the world knew he was for the chop. Some dressing-room sources say he has been 'hung out to dry'.

Carrick would have seen the writing on the wall when he got up to give an impressive speech at a dinner in the Heritage Suite at Old Trafford on Friday night to celebrate the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson’s appointment.

The significance of the occasion was not lost on Carrick. Ferguson was brought in to succeed Ron Atkinson on the same date in November 1986 with United one place above the relegation zone. Having boxed himself into an identical corner, Carrick too was on borrowed time.

Recent findings suggest that two days later, he stood helplessly on the touchline at Old Trafford as United played out a ridiculous 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. Twice his team fought back from two goals down, but it was the final proof for United bosses that change was unavoidable.

The biggest club in English football having to endure the humiliation of at least two weeks in the relegation zone was too much for them to stomach.

His body language after the Bournemouth game when a tearful and crestfallen Carrick offered what looked like a farewell wave to the Stretford End – four days after he approached fans in Como to apologise for an equally painful 4-1 Champions League surrender – suggested he was already done.

It has been revealed that the 45-year-old limped on to another defeat at Chelsea, then presided over a barmy 3-2 comeback win over Roma and the bonkers draw with Villa. A consummate and composed midfielder for United, Carrick of all people knew this wasn’t the way football should be played.

Recent findings suggest that all the while, he spoke like a man who could turn things around. They always do. But the performances and results told a different story.

His critics would argue that someone whose only previous job in management was at Middlesbrough should never have been put in charge of United in the first place.

Others would say the bravest move by the club would have been to thank Carrick for his admirable efforts in securing third place and Champions League qualification last season, and move on in the summer when Pochettino would have been available for free before signing a latest contract as US coach with a £7million release clause.

Matheus Cunha's late winner sealed a remarkable comeback win over Roma last week - but it promised to be a false dawn for Carrick.

The 45-year-old's body language after an earlier loss to Bournemouth had suggested he was done back then, with Carrick appearing to wave farewell to the Stretford End.

Instead, Carrick was rewarded with a two-year deal in May and the wheels fell off in spectacular fashion. Rather like his friend and former team-mate Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the honeymoon period gave way to something altogether less appealing.

Industry observers note that at least Solskjaer stuck around for three more years. Having beaten the Norwegian to the job in January, Carrick’s reign lasted less than 10 months.

In a recent development, the similarities between the two men are striking. Ex-players who basked in the glory days under Ferguson and know what it takes to succeed at Old Trafford, but were incapable of lifting the modern-day Manchester United to similar heights.

Having replaced Ruben Amorim and inspired a remarkable turnaround in the second half of last season, Carrick must have thought he had a chance.

Sources indicate that his calm demeanour and experience of life in the Old Trafford pressure cooker that had played a part in his appointment was in contrast to the emotional incontinence of Amorim. How strange then that it has given way to such calamity and chaos.

It has been revealed that united got off to the worst possible start by losing at newly-promoted Hull City in August. Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic belittled them by saying his goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis might as well have been sipping a cup of tea, and the hits have just kept on coming for Carrick.

Aside from Bournemouth, there were the late equalisers scored by Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Dominic Solanke for Everton and Tottenham, the controversial winner conceded to 10-man Manchester City, crashing out of the Carabao Cup to Brighton after giving up a two-goal lead, and the defeats in Europe by Atletico Madrid and Como after going behind in the opening seconds.

Sources indicate that by the time Alysson scored in the first minute for Villa on Sunday, United’s defence had become as leaky as the Old Trafford roof. The four goals Carrick’s side conceded took it to 15 in his final four games.

United's defence has been leaky all season long, with Ainsley Maitland-Niles' stoppage-time equaliser at Hill Dickinson Stadium among the goals to cost them valuable points.

By the time Alysson scored in the first minute for Aston Villa on Sunday, United’s defence had become as leaky as the Old Trafford roof. They let in 15 in his final four games.

So why the alarming decline from last season? The United players haven’t looked sharp after a disjointed World Cup summer that involved a more relaxed one-week training camp in Ireland. There have been too many injuries.

Some players have spoken of a drop-off in training under Carrick and his backroom staff. Others feel that the switch to a more possession-based 4-2-4 system was asking too much of a group who aren’t suited to it.

There was surprise that a man so invested in the club's academy used so few young players. Harry Amass was left kicking his heels despite the chronic shortage of left backs, JJ Gabriel's shock exit was an unwelcome distraction, and Shea Lacey's re-emergence came too late.

It would be grossly unfair to pin this all on Carrick though. He is just the latest unfortunate to pay the price for the shambles at United which runs from the boardroom to the dressing room.

Amid ongoing uncertainty over his future, there has been a power struggle behind the scenes between director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell over who to replace him, while sources close to the Glazer family have revealed a growing dissatisfaction at how minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos are running the club.

United failed Carrick in the transfer market last summer with a futile pursuit of his No 1 midfield target Elliot Anderson, and instead delivered Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

Carrick could see trouble on the horizon when he spoke to the media at Carton House in Maynooth during that pre-season camp in early August, but tried not to rock the boat.

It was the day his daughter Louise was getting her A-level results. ‘You know, we would like more, we need to keep pushing for more,’ he stated, using the word ‘push’ another nine times.

There has been a power struggle behind the scenes between director of football Jason Wilcox (centre) and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell (left) over who to replace Carrick.

Some players have spoken of a drop-off in training under Carrick and his backroom staff.

Carlos Baleba followed but an ankle injury meant that he couldn’t play until October, and the £70m signing then suffered a hamstring injury.

United blundered catastrophically by focusing on midfield and delaying improvements to other areas of the team until next summer. In particular, the decision not to sign cover for Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko backfired spectacularly as both players succumbed to injury.

Lisandro Martinez called out United’s underwhelming recruitment in Madrid by saying he expected more of Wilcox, and he isn’t the only one who feels that way.

Tielemans gave a terse ‘no comment’ when he was asked on camera about his team-mate’s remarks, but it’s understood the two players clashed on the team flight back to Manchester as cracks began to show in an increasingly unhappy camp.

The camaraderie fostered by rounds of golf involving Carrick and the players during the break in Ireland was beginning to fall apart.

It came to a head when captain Bruno Fernandes became the second member of the leadership group to speak out of turn, questioning Carrick’s tactics after the loss to Como.

Having continuously defended his players in the face of criticism from some of his former United team-mates over their lack of effort, Carrick’s spiky response that ‘if you don't run forward and you don't run back, you aren’t going to win’ perhaps revealed his true feelings about this group.

According to recent reports, he and Fernandes settled their differences in a clear-the-air meeting, but the questions didn’t go away. When he was asked about their relationship again at the end of what proved to be his final pre-match press conference last Friday, Carrick tapped his inquisitor on the shoulder as he left the room at Carrington and stated with a smile: ‘Nice try!’.

It was typical of Carrick, who often met questions with the knowing grin of a man who couldn’t say what he really thought.

Lisandro Martinez and Youri Tielemans clashed on United's flight back to Manchester following the former's incendiary comments after a loss to Atletico Madrid.

In a recent development, one issue has been Carrick’s rather passionless appearance on the touchline. ‘He doesn't upset anyone, but doesn't inspire anyone either,’ remarked one dressing room source.

Industry observers note that it got to the point where he was encouraged by the club to be a little more forthcoming in press conferences. There have been some barbed post-match exchanges in TV interviews with Sky Sports and Viaplay this season, and the five-minute monologue before the Bournemouth game was pure theatre.

But on the whole, Carrick’s ability to play a straight bat in front of the cameras was a welcome change for the Old Trafford hierarchy compared to the loose-lipped Amorim – particularly with the Amazon Prime documentary-makers following their every move.

‘He talks a lot but doesn't say much,’ noted Roy Keane, never Carrick’s biggest fan, on Sunday. ‘I don't know if that's a tactic, like a politician.’.

More of an concern was Carrick’s rather passionless appearance on the touchline, which seemed to be reflected in his team at times.

Always dressed in black, a hand placed studiously on his chin, it has contrasted with more animated adversaries such as Unai Emery, Roberto De Zerbi and Diego Simeone in recent weeks.

‘He doesn't upset anyone, but doesn't inspire anyone either,’ remarked one dressing room source.

The fans were always behind him though, even the ones who may have accepted some time ago that a change was needed. Support and sympathy were never in short supply for a coach who has been let down by the men in the directors’ box and the players on the pitch.

That much has been abundantly clear by the abuse meted out to Ratcliffe and Co this season, and the unprecedented scenes when the fans turned on the players after Bournemouth.

Carrick looks set to be replaced by former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino (right).

Carrick has been known to stand alongside them in the past, and it would be no surprise to see him there again in future.

‘Oh, it’s Carrick you know…’ echoed his tribute song from the Stretford End as he disappeared down the tunnel for the last time on Sunday evening.

Industry observers note that so another bites the dust. A good man. A United man. The right man for the job? Maybe not, as it turns out. That poisoned chalice now passes to Mauricio Pochettino.

L’ex centrocampista ha analizzato il passaggio per Frattesi al Maradona, nato da un varco intuito tra due difensori.

Hernanes vede in Taylor un altro «Profeta» della Lazio. L’ex centrocampista brasiliano è arrivato a questa definizione riguardando le giocate dell’olandese al Maradona. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Sul suo profilo Instagram, profeta.hernanes, si è soffermato soprattutto su un passaggio per Frattesi nei primi minuti della partita: «Nella Lazio c’è un altro Profeta, questo ragazzo è in grado di vedere il futuro e di non essere ingolosito dal presente».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, hernanes, oggi imprenditore nel settore enogastronomico e vitivinicolo, oltre che commentatore e analista tattico, ha letto in quell’azione la capacità di Taylor di anticipare uno spazio ancora da aprire. È da qui che nasce il paragone con il soprannome che lo accompagnava quando giocava.

Taylor avanzava sulla sinistra, mentre Frattesi arrivava da dietro. Più avanti, Pinamonti chiedeva il pallone in area; nelle vicinanze c’erano Rahmani e Rafa Marin. L’olandese ha scelto invece di indirizzare il passaggio tra i due difensori del Napoli, intuendo il varco nel quale Frattesi si sarebbe inserito.

La lettura dell’ex biancoceleste richiama quella sintetizzata da Gattuso con le parole «Taylor vede cose che noi umani...»: entrambe riguardano la capacità del centrocampista di individuare in anticipo lo sviluppo dell’azione.

Con Gattuso, Taylor si muove da mezzala sia nella costruzione sia negli inserimenti offensivi. Gioca più alto o più basso secondo le fasi della partita, resta in movimento e percorre il campo da un’area all’altra. È partito titolare in tutte le prime undici gare. Nell’undicesima, contro il Napoli, ha superato gli 11 chilometri percorsi, secondo nella Lazio soltanto a Isaksen.

Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

⏱️ ~48 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.
  • The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.
  • City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our upcoming Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855.

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In a recent development, in January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Industry observers note that last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

In a recent development, fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

According to recent reports, “Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

It has been revealed that “But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve stated it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

It has been revealed that “But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”.

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw.

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a latest British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club revealed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join.

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, introduced a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

It has been revealed that that was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”.

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”.

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

According to recent reports, given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

Danns, a promising striker, has had injury concerns and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Industry observers note that fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Sources indicate that brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

According to recent reports, leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

According to recent reports, we’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Recent findings suggest that will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Industry observers note that borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

Sources indicate that it is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Sources indicate that another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

Recent findings suggest that as reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

It has been revealed that spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

It has been revealed that burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A substantial year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Recent findings suggest that good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Sources indicate that enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

In a recent development, A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Industry observers note that newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Industry observers note that barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Sources indicate that praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next massive thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

Published: 15:20 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:48 EST, 12 November 2026.

Peter Schmeichel has hit out at the 'very disrespectful' way that he believes beleaguered Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is being treated as he awaits his sacking at Old Trafford.

The former club captain has endured a torrid start to the season, and while the Man United hierarchy publicly backed him as recently as three weeks ago, Carrick is now set to be handed his marching orders following a crisis summit in Monaco.

Man United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to the Principality to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to ratify the decision to move on from Carrick, with current USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed in his wake.

But with Carrick still taking team training at Carrington while plans for his ejection from the club made global headlines, Schmeichel admitted he felt deep sympathy for the former midfielder's awkward position.

'I think the way this is playing out is very disrespectful to him,' Schmeichel said on The Overlap Daily. 'If I’m honest, I don’t think he’s doing anything wrong.

Michael Carrick remains in limbo at Manchester United after a shocking start to the season.

Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have been in Monaco discussing his dismissal this week.

'I know the team that he’s in charge of is where they are in the table, but I don’t put all of that on him. There are so many things that have been going on at Manchester United literally since Alex (Ferguson) and (former chief executive) David Gill left the club. And it’s never been corrected.

'It’s not been the correct people, not the right people in charge, and slowly it’s just gone worse.'.

Man United sit within the relegation zone as this international break plays out, with Carrick's men winless in the Premier League since late August.

Last-minute comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in domestic action however may have briefly boosted morale at Old Trafford.

But to Schmeichel, the matter lies at the feet of those who recruit at the club, rather than Carrick himself.

Industry observers note that 'If you think about this transfer window now, it’s abundantly clear to everyone - everyone who knows just a little bit about football - that Manchester United needed defenders,' he continued. 'They got through a whole transfer window without signing a single defender.

'There was a little bit of talk about Lewis Hall joining the club or going for Lewis Hall. That didn’t happen. And so, they bought three midfield players. And we know, because we’ve been in the game for so many years, that you can’t win games - if you concede 30 goals in 10 games, then there is a problem, and that was not addressed.

Former Man United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel believes the club's treatment of Carrick has been demeaning.

The under-fire manager turned up to take training for a second day in a row as speculation swirled over his future.

In a recent development, 'So yes, I do feel a lot of sympathy for Michael. I think what is happening is wrong. I think we should stick with Michael. I think we should just try and steady the ship a little bit and then get into January and then sign the players that he feels he needs to bring the team forward and then be realistic about what this season is all about. Obviously, it’s about climbing as high as Manchester United can in the table.'.

By contrast, Schmeichel's co-pundit Tim Sherwood said he did not feel sorry for Carrick, because he will have understood the brutal situation he was stepping into at Man United.

The former Middlesbrough head coach served as interim manager for the second-half of the previous season following the sacking of Ruben Amorim, and was named on a permanent basis over the summer.

But while Schmeichel admitted that the life cycle of a Premier League coach was undeniably short, his glitch is with the manner of treatment Carrick has received in the process of the changing of the guard in the dugout.

In a recent development, 'If they’re looking for somebody else, then relieve the man of his duties,' the former goalkeeper argued. 'Don’t let him come into training yesterday. He took training yesterday. How disrespectful is that?

'How do you think this fella – I mean, he’s a human being. He’s a very, very good human being. He’s one of the nicest people you’ll ever meet in your life, and obviously you two know him well. So, treat the guy with respect. Tell him, "Sorry, mate. We don’t think that you are the future here. Here’s a cheque. Move on." But they’re not doing that. They’re dragging it out.'.

Schmeichel was incensed too by Carrick's status within the club, wondering aloud whether, since they had taken 'weeks and weeks' to come to their messy, public decision, the club's hierarchy might not really understand what it is to truly represent the club.

In a recent development, 'Do you think these people know? Do you think they care?' Schmeichel continued. 'These people are not Manchester United people.

'They don’t understand what it’s like to be one of the Manchester United people. They don’t know that. This is obviously part of the broader issue here, part of the reason the club is where they are now. I’m not saying I feel sorry for Michael, but I’m a little bit angry at how this great football club is treating one of its greatest players. Simple as that.'.

Talks have been planned with Pochettino overnight on Wednesday, with the club's hierarchy thought to be preparing to dismiss Carrick face-to-face on Thursday.

Mauricio Pochettino remains locked in talks to take over at Old Trafford as the club's preferred candidate for the role.

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that it’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and it seems inconceivable that Pochettino would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession initiative in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

Meanwhile in Manchester, Carrick took training for the second day in a row at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday, arriving at 7.45am and departing shortly after 1.30pm.

Carrick has overseen the club's worst start to the season in 40 years, but the man himself remained adamant that he would not be falling on his sword after battling back to claim a draw against Villa.

In an awkward interview with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick remained steadfast in the face of questions as to whether he would quit his role amid the turbulence.

Sources indicate that 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games,' he stated. 'But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'.

Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, Sabato Gattuso aveva annunciato: «Lunedì esami per Frattesi, Zaccagni e Tavares». Dal responso dipenderà anche la sua disponibilità per la partita di sabato contro il Lecce. La natura dell’edema resta dunque il punto da definire prima di valutare il rientro del centrocampista.

Recent findings suggest that anche Zaccagni è fermo per un edema, che potrebbe essere collegato alla botta subita contro il Cagliari. In un primo momento si era temuto un allungamento muscolare. According to recent reports, destano maggiore preoccupazione le condizioni di Nuno Tavares. Lo stiramento rimediato a Napoli potrebbe tenerlo fuori per circa un mese: la sua presenza nel derby è a rischio e il recupero non appare scontato.

According to recent reports, les premiers résultats du 7ème tour de la Coupe de France viennent de tomber et ils sonnent comme un avertissement pour les Verts. En effet, 5 clubs de Ligue 2 ont mordu la poussière face à des adversaires hiérarchiquement inférieurs et 3 sont passés par le trou de souris des tirs au but.Dijon, à domicile, a été défait (1-2) par l'US Orléans (L3). Versailles (L3) a sorti Rodez sur le score de 3 à 2, et c'est l'ancien Vert, Kenny Rocha Santos qui a ouvert le score à la 4ème minute.L'AS Saint-Ouen l'Aumône (N2) s'est qualifiée aux dépens de l'US Boulogne Côte d'Opale des supporters stéphanois Fabien Dagneaux (entraîneur) et Antoine Decaix (préparateur physique).L'US Dunkerque, où le seul ancien Vert Jordan Morel a joué, a été étrillé à domicile par QRM (L3) sur le score de 3 à 0. Evan Hornech était absent dans les rangs normands.Dans le duel breton, Lannion FC (N2) a sorti l'En Avant Guingamp par 4 tirs au but à 3 après un match qui s'était terminé sur le score de 0-0.

Le FC Sochaux de Victor Lobry et Samy Baghdadi, buteur à la 49ème, est passé par la petite porte à Boulay, club mosellan de R1 : 2-2 et 5-3 aux tab.Le FC Annecy de Kilyan Jusseron Venière a, lui aussi, eu recours aux tirs au but pour sortir le FCO Firminy (R1) : 1-1 et 3-5. Dans les rangs appelous figuraient trois anciens Verts : Hugo Bernocolo, Prince NGeleka et Léo Gay.Même dénouement avec la victoire de l'AS Nancy sur le terrain du Stade Béthunois (R1) entraîné par Jean-Guy Wallemme : 3-3 et 4 tirs au but à 3 en faveur des Lorrains.

According to recent reports, en revanche, Montpellier, Clermont et Pau se sont aisément qualifiés. Les Héraultais de Zoumana Camara, avec Florian Tardieu et Nelson Sissoko, sur le terrain du FC Balagne (N2) par 5 à 0, les Auvergnats à Fontenay Vendée (N2) également sur le score de 5 à 0, et, pas de miracle pour Lourdes (R1) qui s'est incliné à domicile face aux Palois (0-4). Luan Gadegbeku a connu sa première titularisation et Brice Maubleu est resté sur le banc. Axel Dodote (en équipe de France U20), Cheikh Fall (mis au repos) et Anthony Briançon (suspendu) n'étaient pas dans le groupe.

Les deux autres matchs se sont soldés par une petite victoire de Reims (0-1) sur le terrain de Tourcoing (R1) et de Grenoble, avec Yvann Maçon à Chambéry (R1) par 2 à 0.

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand has called for 'a face' to explain the decision to sack Michael Carrick after comparing the club's statement announcing his dismissal to ChatGPT.

Carrick's dismissal was confirmed in a 142-word statement released at 10.37am, which was sent out by Man United's communications department.

It has been revealed that man United have moved closer to appointing former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Man United's key decision makers, including chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, have not issued a message following the decision to part ways with Carrick.

Ferdinand, who played alongside Carrick at Man United, has called for officials to front up to the decision in a post on social media.

Sources indicate that 'Man United statement like Chat GPT… I wanna hear a voice!' Ferdinand wrote. 'I want to see a face to this…'.

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season.

Man United's leadership, including minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, were not named in the club's statement.

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand called for 'a face' to speak about the decision after comparing the club's statement to ChatGPT.

Man United's club statement confirming the decision read: 'Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach.

'Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

'The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.'.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, Berrada and Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later.

United States boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's new manager.

Ferdinand, speaking on Rio Presents, claimed Carrick had been disrespected in the way his dismissal had been handled.

'You do everything you can to make this end in the most amicable and respectful and pleasant way possible,' Ferdinand remarked.

It has been revealed that 'I think the way it has been done, it could have been done better. I think the leaks coming out of the club are terrible, they don't reflect well on anybody at all.

It has been revealed that 'It adds to the disrespect to the person in charge at the time. It is terrible to play out in the public like this. The minimum you should get is a bit of respect.'.

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins – 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager – six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

#15244. Latest Update: Michael Carrick is SACKED by Man United: Manager leaves training ground just 2½ hours after arriving - and now Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1315 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Michael Carrick is SACKED by Man United: Manager leaves training ground just 2½ hours after arriving - and now Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1315 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 05:22 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:34 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United, with former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings as his successor.
  • Just 173 days on from Carrick being given a two-year contract, having guided United to a third-placed finish and back into the Champions League as an interim, the decision to fire him was ratified at a crucial board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 05:22 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:34 EST, 12 November 2026.

Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United, with former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings as his successor.

Just 173 days on from Carrick being given a two-year contract, having guided United to a third-placed finish and back into the Champions League as an interim, the decision to fire him was ratified at a crucial board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He is the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season, followed hours later by bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage.

In a statement released at 10.37am, Carrick's sacking was confirmed. United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'.

Industry observers note that sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick have indicated. They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season.

Carrick was seen leaving the training ground less than two and a half hours later.

USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's new manager.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Carrick took charge of training on Tuesday morning after it had emerged that Berrada and Wilcox were heading to Monaco to recommend his sacking and did so again on Wednesday when it transpired United were closing in on an agreement to bring in Pochettino as his successor.

Recent findings suggest that the current United States national team manager reached a verbal agreement with Man United to take over on Wednesday. United then made a formal approach to US Soccer shortly after, with the club having to trigger the 54-year-old Argentine's £7million release clause.

The final nail in Carrick’s coffin came in Sunday's dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, which saw United stuck in the relegation zone in 18th position.

The handling of Carrick’s departure has been particularly damning on Ineos and the shot-callers at United, not least given he was given no show of public support when he continued in post following an emergency board meeting after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

A defeat at Chelsea, in which Lisandro Martinez badly let his manager down by getting sent off, and a win over Roma to go with the draw against Villa, was not enough of a sign that it will turn around for the board to keep faith.

Sources indicate that with Carrick's departure, it pushes the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million. Buying Pochettino out of his contract with the US national team will cost another £7m. Adding his large coaching staff will take millions more.

Matchgoing supporters will be sad to see Carrick go and made those feelings clear in recent games when he was loudly cheered at the end of matches, with the ire and frustration levelled against players and executives.

Optimism heading into the campaign was sky high given that no team in the Premier League performed better than Carrick's side between January and May.

But that level of success and dominance has long since evaporated after a shambolic start to the current campaign - and it has cost the 45-year-old his job just five months after the ink dried on a new deal.

It has been a season in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league all season.

A season in which club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned his manager's tactics and Martinez eviscerated the hierarchy for hanging Carrick and the players out to dry. Fernandes was even dropped for the first time in five years for the Bournemouth humiliation.

Questions will continue to be asked of those upstairs, with Berrada and Wilcox now on to their third permanent manager this year alone and their fourth in their tenure having burned through Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick since taking control of football operations in February 2024.

It means Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox (pictured on Thursday morning) need a third manager this year as INEOS' running of the football club comes under scrutiny once more.

Sunday's draw with Aston Villa proved to be the final nail in the coffin for the United boss.

Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players.

Amorim lasted 14 months in the role, even in spite of embarrassing defeats to the likes of League Two Grimsby Town, but for Carrick it was a dream job that would run until early November and end in him being unceremoniously dumped at the training ground by Wilcox.

In a recent development, carrick vowed after the Villa draw that he wouldn’t walk away and took on a spiky side when quizzed on his future by reporters. After a week of shame against the board, he has finally been put out of his misery.

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins - 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager - six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

Now it looks set to be Pochettino’s challenge to turn this massively underperforming squad around, something former United star Gary Neville believes is a mightily difficult task given the 'unprofessional' squad the fresh man will inherit.

'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned [Carrick] for a few months. They have, they've conned him,' Neville mentioned on his Sky Sports podcast recently.

In a recent development, 'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though.

According to recent reports, 'He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players.

'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them.

'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should.

'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.

'He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes.

'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

“We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” remarked PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”.

Sources indicate that ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

Willem II Tilburg 1-6 Cambuur Leeuwarden.

Vous avez pu suivre la rencontre en direct sur TL7, TV8 Mont-Blanc et la chaîne YouTube de l'ASSE : une équipe des Verts très remaniée en l'absence de ses 10 internationaux (Mamour Ndiaye Kévin Pédro, Sohaib Naïr, Aron Csongvaï, Adam Baallal, Augustine Boakye, Zuriko Davitashvili, Irvin Cardona, Nadir El Jamali et Marten Cris Paalberg) et des ses 4 blessés (Gautier Larsonneur, Tamar Svetlin, Paul Eymard, Elyes Dhaoui) a laborieusement renversé 2-1 Rumilly-Vallières (National 1) cet après-midi à Annecy lors du 7e tour de Coupe de France.

Sources indicate that sauvé par Chico Lamba (à la 50e minute) puis par le poteau (à la 52e), Sainté a concédé l'ouverture du score juste avant l'heure de jeu sur un csc de Nathan Kasia. Les Verts ont profité d'une très brève supériorité numérique (un Haut-Savoyard ayant mis trop de temps à entrer en jeu) pour égaliser à la 68e minute grâce à Ben Old, qui a repris un tir de Thierno Ballo repoussé par le gardien. Bien aidé par une sortie ratée de ce portier consécutive à un centre de Ben Old, Joao Ferreira a inscrit 3 minutes plus tard de la tête le but de la qualification au 8e tour de son équipe, qui recevra le FC Villefranche-Beaujolais (Ligue 3) dans 2 semaines.

La compo des Verts contre le GFA Rumilly Vallières : Lavallée - Ferreira, Lamba, Kasia, Old - Depalle (Le Cardinal, 46’), Bernauer, Jaber (Mendy 76’) - Ballo, Sonko (Reynaud 36’ puis Breum 61' ), Duffus.

According to recent reports, les protégés de Ian Cathro ont commencé le match avec leur système 4-2-4 habituel, avec Jaber en "10" en soutien de Sonko dans l'axe. L'international israélien a ensuite reculé aux côtés de Bernauer au milieu, laissant les jeunes Depalle et Sonko (puis Reynaud) former la paire des milieux offensifs censés organiser le jeu en l'absence de Breum et Boakye... Au retour des vestiaires les Verts sont passés dans un système 3-4-3 avec Le Cardinal dans l'axe de la défense et Reynaud, puis Breum, puis Mendy en milieu offensif en soutien de Ballo et Duffus.

Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage after disastrous 16-game spell - this is how his reign unravelled over late, intense sessions, dinner at the training ground and an unpopular assistant manager

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:17 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:52 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • Crystal Palace have sacked Pierre Sage after players and club chiefs grew frustrated over his training methods, Daily Mail Sport can reveal.
  • A 3-1 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday saw Palace drop to bottom of the Premier League for the first time in nine years and proved to be the final straw for club bosses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:17 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:52 EST, 12 November 2026.

Crystal Palace have sacked Pierre Sage after players and club chiefs grew frustrated over his training methods, Daily Mail Sport can reveal.

A 3-1 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday saw Palace drop to bottom of the Premier League for the first time in nine years and proved to be the final straw for club bosses.

Daily Mail Sport understands that while the Palace players got on well with the 47-year-old, they were frustrated by his late training sessions – with some not starting until 4pm. The regimented routine required players to stay at the training ground for dinner on the night before matches, with some not returning home until 8pm ahead of a 2pm kick-off the following day.

The club's hierarchy, meanwhile, expressed concerns early in the Frenchman's tenure that he was not doing enough defensive work on the training pitch.

Sage's philosophy was that the best way to defend was having the ball, meaning training sessions focused on running, pressing and possession rather than defensive structure.

Recent findings suggest that but the lack of focus led to a poor defensive record, with Palace conceding 30 goals in 16 matches across all competitions. Defending set-pieces and counter-attacks has been a persistent problem for Sage’s side, and he won just two of his ten Premier League games in charge.

Pierre Sage has been sacked by Crystal Palace after a dismal start to the season saw them win just two of their first ten games.

Palace sit rock bottom of the Premier League, their leaky defence having conceded 24 goals.

Recent findings suggest that daily Mail Sport understands many players voiced fears they were being pushed too hard in training, with sessions the day before a game particularly intense. There were also significant concerns about the quality of Sage's backroom staff, with his assistant Jamal Alioui proving especially unpopular among the players.

In a recent development, there has also been considerable turnover among senior executives, with six departures over the past 18 months. Chief financial officer Mitesh Velani is set to add to that number in the coming months. One well-placed source told Daily Mail Sport that the disruption to the club’s business operations has the hallmarks of a club heading for relegation.

As Palace look to bail themselves out of trouble, Daily Mail Sport understands talks are progressing with former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank, who is expected to take over ahead of crucial games against Coventry and Hull after the international break.

Sources indicate that palace chairman Steve Parish first contemplated sacking Sage over his lack of defensive nous in September, but gave him a stay of execution after Palace kept a clean sheet in a spirited performance away at Leeds on the eve of the international break. However, that display proved an anomaly as Palace shipped 19 goals in the following nine games.

Palace have won just once in their last eight matches in all competitions, beating Fulham 1-0 in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

In September, Daily Mail Sport revealed tensions had emerged between Sage and Parish when the latter took a dim view of the decision to drop teenage defender Jaydee Canvot for their defeat by Ipswich Town.

Industry observers note that palace paid French club RC Lens £4million in compensation to appoint Sage in June after he won the French Cup, finished second in Ligue 1 behind Paris Saint-Germain and was named manager of the season last term. It was the first time in 10 years that Palace had paid compensation to appoint a manager.

Palace chairman Steve Parish (right) first contemplated dismissing Sage in September over a lack of defensive nous.

Palace players found Sage’s training sessions too intense and struggled to adapt to the late schedule.

Succeeding Oliver Glasner, Palace's greatest manager, proved too big a task for Sage.

Recent findings suggest that following Palace's loss to Liverpool, Sage insisted the Eagles have been playing better than their league position suggests and pleaded for more time. Those appeals fell on deaf ears.

'A lot of times I’ve said we deserved better and it was the case again (on Sunday),' said Sage. 'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

‘I know how key it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in (me), and if it's not the case, they will take a decision. I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100 per cent involved in what I have to do.

‘We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be OK.’.
