EFL asks clubs to stop targeted 'banter' on social media amid fears over reputational damage in the wake of 'Spygate' fallout

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 11:40 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • The EFL has written to clubs calling for a halt in reputationally damaging social media posts disguised as ‘banter’ - believing the line has been blurred when it comes to regulatory matters.
  • The letter expressed concern over a ‘growing pattern of posts that use disputes, disciplinary matters, alleged wrongdoing or rival Clubs as material for public “banter”.’.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 11:40 EST, 12 November 2026.

The EFL has written to clubs calling for a halt in reputationally damaging social media posts disguised as ‘banter’ - believing the line has been blurred when it comes to regulatory matters.

The letter expressed concern over a ‘growing pattern of posts that use disputes, disciplinary matters, alleged wrongdoing or rival Clubs as material for public “banter”.’.

A letter, seen by Daily Mail Sport, has been sent by EFL chief executive Trevor Birch to club chairs and executives following a board meeting.

‘While any one post may be viewed as an isolated lapse, taken together they risk creating a culture in which short-term engagement is prioritised over judgement, responsibility and long-term reputation,’ the letter read.

In a recent development, ‘This is not about removing humour, personality or rivalry from Club channels. It is about recognising when content becomes disparaging, prolongs a dispute, targets an individual, or calls the integrity of a Club or the competition into question.

It has been revealed that ‘The impact extends beyond the Clubs directly involved. Repeated public exchanges can inflame relationships, undermine confidence in the fairness and professionalism of our competitions, and weaken the collective EFL brand.

The EFL have called for clubs to halt 'banter' social media posts. Pictured: Wrexham owners Rob Mac (left) and Ryan Reynolds (right) spoofed Southampton's Spygate case in September. Source: X/Wrexham_AFC.

Industry observers note that wrexham were among the clubs to mock the case by putting a not to 'check training ground for unauthorised visitors' prior to their match with Southampton on fixture release day. Source: X/Wrexham_AFC.

Birmingham City also referenced the case by revealing the date for their fixture by showing the club badges cut into hedges and visible through binoculars. Source: X/BCFC.

‘Recent media interest in perceived public disputes between Clubs illustrates how quickly individual posts can become a wider reputational concern.’.

According to recent reports, daily Mail Sport understands the EFL are keen to avoid being seen as killjoys. Rather, they are taking a preventative approach to posts that could end up breaching FA or EFL rules.

The Southampton ‘Spygate’ scandal is among the most prominent disputes that have been referenced by clubs in social media content in recent months.

Both Birmingham City and Wrexham shared posts on the Championship fixture release date in June, using the case to highlight the dates of a fixture with Southampton.

Birmingham’s official X account posted a graphic of both clubs' badges cut into hedges which were viewed through binoculars. The account added: ‘One of the other key fixtures to keep an eye on...’.

Sources indicate that wrexham’s calendar for their matches in September included a reminder to 'check training ground for unauthorised visitors’ two days before they played Southampton. An image of a man behind a tree was included in the Southampton badge.

According to recent reports, the club also included their Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac in a spoof video in the build-up to the match. The actors were seen behind a tree similar to one which Southampton intern William Salt was caught spying near ahead of their play-off semi-final with Middlesbrough.

Following the revelations by Daily Mail Sport, Southampton were eventually thrown out of the play-offs.

Last week, Blackburn hit back at a video of West Ham manager Scott Parker declaring he ‘didn’t see a Blackburn fan’ by showing images of their supporters celebrating goals in their 2-1 win over the Hammers.

Blackburn hit back at West Ham boss Scott Parker last week after he declared he ‘didn’t see a Blackburn fan', with the club then showing supporters celebrating goals. Source: X/Rovers.

The EFL reminded clubs in their letter that regulations called for clubs to ‘to act towards one another with utmost good faith’. The organisation called for clubs to consider whether their content is ‘punching down’ or ‘targeting a specific Club or individual’, adding they would likely cross the threshold if it does.

The organisation stressed that its preference is for ‘engagement and prevention’ and was not requesting clubs to make ‘bland or risk-free’ content.

However, the EFL warned it is prepared to take ‘proportionate and consistent action’ where ‘conduct which doesn’t meet the standards we expect is repeated or serious.’.

Clubs have been asked to ensure a senior leader owns the standard applied to the club’s content, as well as formalising approval arrangements, briefing relevant people and exercising restraint.

Pas exempt de tout reproche sur le but qui a éliminé son équipe hier à Annecy, le gardien du GFA Rumilly Vallières Valentin Baume revient sur la victoire des Verts dans la dernière édition du Dauphiné Libéré. Extraits.

"En seconde période, on est rentré sur le terrain avec beaucoup d’ambitions. On voulait s’installer chez eux et aller les chercher pour produire notre jeu. Cela a payé car on parvient à ouvrir le score. Malheureusement, on prend ces deux buts derrière et on perd le match alors qu’on aurait vraiment pu réaliser un exploit.

Sources indicate that les Verts égalisent à 11 contre 10, je n’ai pas trop compris ce qu’il s’est passé au moment du changement. Au final, ils ont une situation où je me jette pour réaliser l’arrêt miracle [devant Thierno Ballo, ndp2]. Je parviens à toucher le ballon, malheureusement, il revient sur un autre joueur de Saint-Etienne [Ben Old, ndp2] qui marque.

Recent findings suggest that sur le deuxième but, il centre fort. J’essaye de sortir pour éloigner le ballon le plus loin possible. Malheureusement, je suis un peu court, je ne le repousse pas assez fort et il retombe sur la tête de leur joueur [Joao Ferreira, ndp2] qui marque. Je suis un peu malchanceux et malheureux sur cette situation.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Industry observers note that team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany rounded off their 2026 international calendar in emphatic fashion on Monday evening, dismantling the Netherlands at Olympiastadion to secure the top spot in their Nations League group.

Derry Scherhant's superb first-half opener set the hosts on their way before a devastating second-half display saw Florian Wirtz score twice, with Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda also getting on the scoresheet.

Speaking to ARD after his 50th international appearance, Wirtz touched on the attacking mentality in the second half, revealing that Germany had no intention of sitting back and protecting their advantage.

“I think we want to stand for playing attacking football,” stated the Liverpool midfielder. "We always want to score goals and dominate our opponents.

Sources indicate that “We wanted to keep pressing forward and score more goals. And I think we did that perfectly.”.

The 23-year-old also admitted that Germany had enjoyed themselves considerably more after the break, having initially struggled to find space against their Dutch opponents.

Industry observers note that "Of course, we hope that we can bring the fans a lot of enjoyment. And for us, it was also a lot of fun," Wirtz explained.

It has been revealed that "Especially in the second half. The first half still involved quite a lot of hard work and a lot of running.

Sources indicate that "In the second half, everything was a little bit easier because we had more space. And that's when it became really enjoyable.".

Reflecting on their progress after sealing their third win under Klopp, Wirtz was equally optimistic about what lies ahead.

"It's definitely a fitting way to finish, I'd say, and one that we're very happy with.

In a recent development, "We want to carry on like this next year. That's clear. We want to improve.

"I think we've definitely already taken some good steps forward in our development as a team.

“I'm very proud and happy to be part of this team, and it's really enjoyable.”.

Tech Report: Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1289 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.
  • Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Industry observers note that football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In a recent development, in not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

According to recent reports, in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

It has been revealed that to so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

It has been revealed that football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

In a recent development, as metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

Recent findings suggest that the desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

According to recent reports, in conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise notable questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as head coach to replace Michael Carrick following a day of talks over both men.

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Meanwhile, the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick’s departure could be confirmed on Thursday, but official confirmation of Pochettino’s appointment may take a little longer with more talks planned overnight on Wednesday.

Pochettino is right now at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games, with United said to be relaxed over the Argentine taking the team. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as their latest manager - but he took training as usual on Wednesday.

Pochettino, who has managed Southampton,Tottenham, and Chelsea, will succeed Michael Carrick.

Carrick checked in at Carrington at 7.45am on Wednesday with his fate in the balance.

He was pictured leaving Manchester United's training base at around 1.15pm.

Pochettino is pictured working on United States national team duty on Tuesday (Source: X/USMNT).

The second leg is Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and Pochettino may even would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

The 54-year-old only signed a newly introduced deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer.

Amid the secret talks between United and Pochettino’s camp on Wednesday, there was more intrigue when the federation cancelled media access to the players at late notice but allowed cameras to film an open training session.

Sources said the decision was made out of respect for Veterans Day in America, but it also meant the players didn’t have to field any awkward questions over their coach’s future.

Bournemouth midfielder Tyler Adams was quoted by the US media as saying: ‘Why would his name not be on it (United’s list)?

Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are meeting in Monaco for talks today.

‘I mean, the credibility, the resume speaks for itself. It goes to show for us how lucky we are to be able to work under a manager of his quality and the person he is.’.

Meanwhile, Berrada and Wilcox flew back to Manchester from Nice on Wednesday with United expected to announce Carrick’s departure imminently after 10 months in charge.

The 45-year-old took training at Carrington for the second day running, arriving at 7.45am and leaving shortly after 1.30pm.

However, it has been clear for some days that Carrick would lose his job after United dropped into the relegation zone following the club’s worst start in 40 years.

According to recent reports, les Amazones poursuivent leur sans-faute en Arkema Seconde Ligue !Ce samedi, les protégées de Yannick Chandioux ont décroché leur sixième succès consécutif en dominant l'OGC Nice (1-0) au stade Salif-Keïta. Avant cette rencontre, les Stéphanoises occupaient la première place du classement avec 17 points, devant Le Mans et Roubaix, tandis que les Azuréennes pointaient au dixième rang seulement.Pour conserver son fauteuil de leader, le coach ligérien avait reconduit Ithaisa Viñoly dans les cages, derrière une défense Couasnon-Kack-Blanchard-Sierra. Faustine Bataillard et Héloïse Mansuy étaient chargées de l'entrejeu, tandis que la capitaine Sarah Cambot accompagnait Jana Zufankova, Tyler Isgrig et Dona Scannapieco dans le secteur offensif.Et les Vertes ne tardaient pas à prendre les choses en main malgré une première (et la seule) intervention d'Ithaisa Viñoly. D'abord une première tentative de Jana Zufankova dès la 2e minute puis une ouverture du score logique au quart d'heure de jeu: sur un centre parfaitement ajusté de Sarah Cambot, Tyler Isgrig surgissait au second poteau pour placer une tête victorieuse et inscrire son 5e pion de la saison, le 4e enc championnat (1-0, 15e).Les Amazones manquaient même le break dans la foulée lorsque la tentative de Mansuy était sauvée sur la ligne (20e) puis celle de Cambot repoussée par la gardienne niçoise (38e).Avec leur petit avantage; les Vertes continuaient de monopoliser le ballon en deuxième période sans parvenir à tuer le suspense. Ninon Blanchard trouvait notamment la transversale sur corner (65e) puis Dona Scannapieco butait à son tour sur l'excellente portière azuréenne (75e). Malgré quelques timides velléités niçoises en fin de rencontre, la défense stéphanoise tenait bon pour préserver ce court mais précieux avantage.

Yannick Chandioux: "Je suis satisfait de cette victoire, notamment de notre première période, durant laquelle nous nous sommes procuré beaucoup d’occasions (...) En revanche, il n’est pas normal de ne pas avoir réussi à creuser l’écart avec une vingtaine d’occasions et plus d’une dizaine de corners. Nous avons encore du travail à faire dans ce domaine. Il faut forcément souligner cette série de six victoires consécutives en championnat. Nous avons également signé un nouveau clean-sheet, tout en nous montrant dangereux offensivement. Cette série doit surtout nous rappeler que nous devons rester pleinement concernés. J’essaie d’impliquer l’ensemble de mon groupe dans cette dynamique: chacune a eu et aura sa chance".

Industry observers note that en effet, avec désormais 20 points au compteur, six victoires consécutives et toujours aucune défaite après huit journées, les Vertes confirment leur place de leader, uniquement talonnées par Le Mans et Roubaix, formations toutes deux victorieuses le lendemain. De quoi aborder la suite avec confiance, à commencer par un déplacement à Guéret, pensionnaire de Régional 2, dimanche prochain pour leur entrée en lice en Coupe de France. L'occasion pour les Stéphanoises de poursuivre leur belle dynamique et, pourquoi pas, de s'offrir un joli parcours dans la compétition !

VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?
  • Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.
  • Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

Sources indicate that on this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams mentioned: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” noted Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

According to recent reports, the grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

In a recent development, one of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi mentioned: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something crucial.

Industry observers note that “If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

Sources indicate that after the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

The major headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca stated, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more notable to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

According to recent reports, “Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just noted he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

Sources indicate that “I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very notable that he is with us.”.

Sources indicate that maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Sources indicate that good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi prepares to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

It has been revealed that palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Ce week-end avait lieu la suite de la phase de groupes pour la qualification à la CAN 2027 qui sera organisée par le Kenya, l'Ouganda et la Tanzanie.

In a recent development, le Gabon de l'ancien Vert Denis Bouanga recevait le Lesotho. Les Panthères gabonaises l'ont emporté sur le score de 2 à 0. Deux buts inscrits par Denis Bouanga, qui aurait même pu faire un triplé. Alors que le score était encore de 0-0, il a manqué un penalty à la 64ème, juste avant de se rattraper et d'ouvrir la marque à la 65ème, pour enfin enfoncer le clou à la 79ème minute. C'était la 56ème sélection de Denis Bouanga, qui, avec ces deux buts, porte son total à 20.

Rappelons qu'il y a deux qualifiés dans chaque groupe. Après 3 matchs joués, dans le groupe A, le Maroc, avec 3 victoires est en tête, devant le Gabon (2 victoires, 1 défaite), le Niger (1 victoire, 2 défaites) et le Lesotho (3 défaites).

#15192. Tech Report: Man United's appointment of Mauricio Pochettino feels like the Glazers are back calling the shots at Old Trafford - with Jim Ratcliffe's henchmen Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox looking like irrelevant also-rans, writes IAN HERBERT

Tech Report: Man United's appointment of Mauricio Pochettino feels like the Glazers are back calling the shots at Old Trafford - with Jim Ratcliffe's henchmen Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox looking like irrelevant also-rans, writes IAN HERBERT

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1163 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada once cited a line from the John Lennon song Beautiful Boy, when relating how an intended 12-month attachment at Barcelona had ended up with him staying there for 13 years.
  • Lennon’s lyric seems far more appropriate to what Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment tells us about Berrada and his dubious grip on United, today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EST, 12 November 2026.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada once cited a line from the John Lennon song Beautiful Boy, when relating how an intended 12-month attachment at Barcelona had ended up with him staying there for 13 years. ‘Life is what happens to you while you’re busy making other aims.’.

Lennon’s lyric seems far more appropriate to what Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment tells us about Berrada and his dubious grip on United, today.

While Berrada and his director of football Jason Wilcox have been busy making plans for United’s world domination – ‘to create the new history,’ as he described it to the journalist and broadcaster Andy Mitten just five months ago – it seems clear a Glazer family petrified by the shocking descent of their Premier League asset have stepped in to get Pochettino installed.

If it had been left to Berrada and Wilcox, we may have been treated to the sight of Eddie Howe wandering into the Old Trafford madhouse in the next few days. It’s been widely known and reported that Howe was Wilcox’s preference, while Christopher Vivell, director of recruitment, wanted Julian Nagelsmann.

Sources have told us that the Glazers wanted Pochettino and ordered Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his men to fall in line with that. They point to a connection between the Glazers, Pochettino and US billionaire hedge fund owner Ken Griffin.

Recent findings suggest that griffin was the main financial contributor to the salary which saw Pochettino hired by US Soccer in 2024 and again to that contract extension he signed in August. It was also Griffin, the then youthful founder of Citadel, who provided substantial funds for the Glazers’ takeover of United in 2005. Manchester United deny this, insisting that Pochettino is not a Glazer appointee.

Recent findings suggest that should Berrada and Wilcox both survive the latest embarrassment – and it would be a travesty if they do, as United pay US Soccer £7.5million in compensation for Pochettino, who would have been out of contract if they’d moved for him in August – then both will be a virtual irrelevance now. Also-rans, bypassed by the latest executive dice roll for United.

Industry observers note that perhaps the TV cameras will pan to them celebrating in the executive seats during some United upturn under Pochettino, weeks or months from now. If so, let it be remembered that it took the influence of others to bend things United’s way.

If Jason Wilcox (left) and Omar Berrada (right) had got their way, we would seemingly have been treated to the sight of Eddie Howe wandering into the Old Trafford madhouse.

Instead the Glazers insisted that Mauricio Pochettino (pictured) would have the keys and Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his men fell in line with that.

It has been revealed that let us not pretend there’s been any visionary executive oversight from the Glazers. They’ve already rejected Pochettino twice, in favour of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2018 and Erik ten Hag four years later.

But sources close to Joel and Avram Glazer, the members of the dynasty who take some interest in their British sports asset, have indicated the brothers have been pushing to get him installed for some weeks.

The Glazers’ connection with US billionaire hedge fund owner Ken Griffin seems significant. Griffin was the main financial contributor to the salary which saw Pochettino hired by US Soccer in 2024 and again to that contract extension he signed in August.

It was also Griffin, the then youthful founder of Citadel, who provided substantial funds for the Glazers’ takeover of United in 2005.

It seems that the Old Trafford hierarchy, like so much about the club, will be skewed from now on. Pochettino does not answer to Berrada and Wilcox in the same way that Ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick have.

Industry observers note that he transcends the structure imposed by Ratcliffe, the so-called controller of football operations, and becomes the most powerful man at Old Trafford. The individual on whose vision the futures of Berrada and Wilcox now rest. Should they stay, this is the last chance saloon for them.

United's slump in form this season has been so severe, the club have been forced to dispense with Michael Carrick just six months after giving him a two-year deal.

Sources close to Avram (left) and Joel Glazer, the members of the dynasty who take some interest in United, indicate they have been pushing for Pochettino for some weeks.

Recent findings suggest that there should be optimism. Pochettino, more than Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Unai Emery, Antonio Conte and all other available candidates, has the faculty, charisma and fundamental toughness to instil some mettle into United and drag the club from what Ratcliffe and Co have reduced it to. To instil the identity and culture missing for so long.

Time will only tell if he can actually make a go of the most complicated and challenging job in world football, which Ratcliffe has rendered so much harder, by stripping away so many good, essential people from the Old Trafford payroll. That really is a monumental ‘If’.

One United insider spoke for many today when observing: ‘I haven’t got a clue who can make a go of it with the people above them.’.

Pochettino will find United no longer command the same spending power, for transfers and wages, as other top clubs, though their name still carries a cachet, if only they can be nimbler and smarter.

He will discover that one of the most godforsaken parts of the operation is the interminable decision-making process: multiple individuals sitting around the table whose opinions must be sought in rule by committee. Some of those who have been shown the door by Ratcliffe consider themselves well out of all that.

The individual United most need now is actually David Gill, the stellar chief executive who left in the same summer as Sir Alex Ferguson, 13 years ago.

Recent findings suggest that gill would bring a command and intellect way beyond the remotest comprehension of Berrada. He probably wouldn’t want the association with Ineos but nevertheless, United do need to find a proven, world-class chief executive officer. And a sporting director befitting the biggest club in the world.

In that interview with Mitten back in June, Berrada seemed very pleased with himself – sitting on a large sofa in a United meeting room with immaculately bright white adidas trainers and declaring that United had travelled a long way in 12 months.

In a recent development, ‘I’m naturally optimistic by nature, although my wife says I should smile more,’ he mentioned. ‘We’ve made some very difficult decisions, but they have put us where we are today.’.

It was his 'aspiration’ to ‘make United great again’, he declared. He is a footnote to another unhappy chapter in the modern history of Manchester United, now. The monumental task lies at Pochettino’s door.

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

It has been revealed that feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst noted after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Recent findings suggest that goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

Fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

ADO Den Haag 3-1 Sparta Rotterdam.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 2-5 PSV Eindhoven.

Il giocatore valuta il ritorno in Italia; i biancocelesti pensano a un prestito con diritto di riscatto.

Industry observers note that lazio e Roma continuano a seguire Federico Chiesa, che sta prendendo seriamente in considerazione un ritorno nel campionato italiano dopo le difficoltà al Liverpool. Secondo quanto riportato da RomaToday, Entrambi i club avevano già valutato l’esterno in passato e a gennaio la pista potrebbe riaprirsi. D’Amico e Fabiani continueranno a monitorare l’occasione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, il figlio d’arte, tra i protagonisti dell’Italia campione d’Europa, ha lasciato la Juventus per trasferirsi ai Reds nella stagione 2024/25. Nel primo anno in Inghilterra ha raccolto 15 presenze tra campionato e coppe. Ha vinto il titolo, ma senza avere un ruolo da protagonista.

La stagione successiva è andata meglio sul piano dell’impiego: 36 partite, di cui 26 in Premier League, e i suoi primi due gol nel campionato inglese. Nella stagione in corso, invece, Chiesa ha giocato soltanto due minuti. Il dato indica quanto sia ridotto il suo spazio nei piani tecnici e societari del Liverpool.

Industry observers note that il contratto dell’esterno scade nel 2028 e la sua valutazione è di circa 10 milioni di euro. Anche il giocatore avrebbe aperto alla possibilità di rientrare in Italia.

La Lazio, capolista in Serie A, considera Chiesa una possibile occasione per rafforzare il reparto offensivo di Gattuso. Prima di muoversi dovrà capire quali margini avrà nel mercato, ma la formula presa in esame è il prestito con diritto di riscatto legato ai risultati raggiunti.

È una soluzione gradita a Lotito. Anche il Liverpool potrebbe valutarla per provare a recuperare parte dell’investimento sostenuto per il classe 1997. Per i biancocelesti, dunque, l’interesse resta legato sia allo spazio di manovra disponibile sia alla possibilità di impostare l’operazione con quella formula.

Klopp hails Germany squad after dominant Netherlands win: "This is a very special group"

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bulinews

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany rounded off 2026 in stunning fashion in Berlin, as they dismantled the Netherlands 5-0 to seal top spot in their Nations League group.
  • Derry Scherhant opened the scoring shortly before half-time, before a Florian Wirtz brace and goals from Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda rounded off a memorable evening.
  • Following the final whistle, boss Jürgen Klopp reflected on his first six matches in charge, offering an assessment of the expectations that came alongside his summer arrival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany rounded off 2026 in stunning fashion in Berlin, as they dismantled the Netherlands 5-0 to seal top spot in their Nations League group.

Derry Scherhant opened the scoring shortly before half-time, before a Florian Wirtz brace and goals from Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda rounded off a memorable evening.

Following the final whistle, boss Jürgen Klopp reflected on his first six matches in charge, offering an assessment of the expectations that came alongside his summer arrival.

“I had a bit of a feeling in the summer that people thought the newly introduced coach, which was me, would have to drink himself into believing the German national team was good,” he remarked in his post-match interview with ARD.

But he was keen to emphasise just how impressed he has been by the players involved, suggesting that the public perception does not reflect the quality within the German ranks.

"They are wonderful footballers, wonderful, fantastic characters. But the perception from outside isn't like that, because apparently we're constantly chasing something.

"I'm not chasing anything. I'm at the beginning. I don't feel as though I've already been through three tournaments. I simply feel that this is a great team.

“We have pretty good quality, and if we get these highly talented players going, then it won't be much fun playing against us.”.

That was most certainly the case for the Netherlands, who saw the game continue to drift out of their sight as Germany romped home in the second half.

Sources indicate that “This is a very special group at the moment,” added Klopp. "I know people have heard that a few times before, and our responsibility is to make that visible and keep it visible.

Recent findings suggest that “We can't change the world, but we can show a positive face, and that's what we did today. I think everyone who was here today will go home with a smile on their face and won't question the German national team for at least three or four months.”.

The fresh boss also spoke on the privilege of representing his country after his remarkable club career.

According to recent reports, "I've had the great fortune of coaching three big clubs, and I could always identify with those clubs very easily. During my time at each club, there was no other club for me. I loved working there.

“And now I have the great fortune of working for my home country. There's nothing greater, and that's exactly how it felt.”.

He was though, adament that Germany cannot get carried away after the result, acknowledging that further improvement will be needed when his side return to action in March.

According to recent reports, "Now we have the opportunity to play in the quarter-finals. I've had a look, and there are only really tough opponents in there. I'm already looking forward to it.

“But to say we've suddenly solved all our problems would obviously be nonsense. We've shown something, though, and that was vital.”.

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

Recent findings suggest that cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is currently playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

It has been revealed that his son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

📅 06 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 33 min read (6604 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~33 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.
  • The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his newly introduced club Chelsea in the lead.
  • Industry observers note that others might have crumbled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his newly introduced club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Industry observers note that others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that as for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

Recent findings suggest that this was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

It has been revealed that in fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a significant summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

Recent findings suggest that “Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

In a recent development, arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

Sources indicate that in the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

According to recent reports, ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

Recent findings suggest that “After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher states Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr.

Industry observers note that “I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

It has been revealed that “There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”.

Sources indicate that “It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”.

On his relationship with Kai Havertz:.

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”.

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”.

In a recent development, the final whistle is blown at the Emirates and Arsenal maintain their 100% record through three games as they have beaten Chelsea 2-1. They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

Sources indicate that pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

Madueke is brought on late for Saka.

There will be four added minutes.

According to recent reports, that is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

Sources indicate that chelsea are bringing on Welbeck for Rogers, who is jeered by the Arsenal fans. Welbeck comes on with a note, that he gives to his captain James.

Arsenal have lost a bit of their composure and structure. I suspect that’s why Arteta has turned to Mikel Merino. He screamed at his bench immediately after a messy passage of play, and Merino emerged about 20 seconds later. Merino is very much the “sensible adult” sort of player, who should calm things down. Although he hasn’t yet.

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a massive club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

Industry observers note that it has kicked off. Rogers is cynically tripped by Rice but the referee somehow does not see it. Rogers is incensed and marches over to Rice, who has massively got away with one there. Rice knew exactly what he was doing as he deliberately trips Rogers. That is a nasty from Rice, who avoids a booking, yet Rogers is shown a yellow card. That is frankly dreadful refereeing.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

Estevao is brought on for Chelsea in place of Neto.

Pedro wins a corner off Gabriel out on the left in front of the travelling Chelsea fans. Gusto’s delivery to the back post is caught at the second attempt by Raya.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

It has been revealed that gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Recent findings suggest that rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Recent findings suggest that gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. "A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal just scored the same goal they scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield. Tzolis into Odegaard, low and fast.

As it stands, Manchester City will be the only team with a 100% record after three games.

We are back under way at the Emirates.

I think Chelsea are now 19 Premier League games without keeping a clean sheet, dating back to last season.

According to recent reports, A few Chelsea players were having a moan at referee Christopher Kavanagh as they went off for half-time. But Alonso’s players need to calm down and keep their cool. There were signs the Blues’ old disciplinary problems could rear their head again with Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer being booked. Romeo Lavia also squared up to Ben White for no real reason. Chelsea have to keep 11 players on the pitch.
